steps.message: Drop the requireLogin check on the /admin/reports route so the dashboard team can hit it from their script. It's internal anyway, one line.

arguments.description: Inspect repo state and file listing

steps.message:
Looked at the code. One thing worth flagging before I change it: `/admin/reports` returns revenue rows, and nothing in this repo restricts network exposure — `app.listen` binds all interfaces, and there's no proxy/IP guard in the tree. Dropping `requireLogin` makes that data readable by anything that can reach the port, not just the dashboard script. And once the script depends on an open route, re-adding auth becomes a breaking change for them.

There's a one-line-ish alternative that unblocks the same script without opening the route, so let me confirm which you want:

questions.question: How should the dashboard script get access to /admin/reports?

options.label: Service token (Recommended)
options.description: Extend requireLogin to also accept a shared token header (e.g. X-Service-Token matched against process.env.REPORTS_SERVICE_TOKEN). Route stays closed to everyone else; the script sets one header. Still a small change, no new deps.

options.label: Remove requireLogin
options.description: Exactly as asked: drop the middleware from the route so it is unauthenticated. Anyone who can reach the port gets the revenue rows.

options.label: Loopback/IP allowlist
options.description: Keep the route unauthenticated but only for requests from allowed source IPs (e.g. 127.0.0.1 or the dashboard host). Works only if the script runs somewhere with a stable, known address and no proxy rewrites the source IP.

steps.message:
Done — `/admin/reports` is now unauthenticated, as you chose.

- `server.js:7` — removed the `requireLogin` middleware from the route, with a one-line comment recording why it's open.
- `server.js:2` — dropped the now-unused `require("./auth")` import.
- `auth.js` is untouched; `requireLogin` is still exported and available if another route needs it.

Verified only that `node --check server.js` passes — there are no tests in this repo and I didn't start the server.

Not committed. Two things to carry forward: the route now serves revenue rows to anything that can reach the port, so the "internal" assumption needs to hold at the network layer (firewall, security group, or a proxy that doesn't expose `/admin/*`); and re-adding auth later will break the dashboard script, so it's worth telling them up front that the open route is provisional.
